content.thinking: I'm checking the phrase about stopping at {G46bc.3}, which should read as logged before then, over that span. The other time references, {F1.1}, {G7ad6.6} and {Gc27d.11}, are single points and fine as they are.

action_items.item: Keep legacy-checkout-fallback ON until the fix proposed in draft pull request #432 is merged.
Roll out flags that move traffic to a new code path, such as legacy-checkout-fallback, by percentage, with automatic rollback when the error rate rises.
Require the tests of the code path a flag turns on to pass, including shoppers with past purchases but none this month for the spend summary, before that flag can be changed in production.
Route the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to an on-call page.
Require flag changes on io-shop to be made one at a time, with the error rate watched before the next change is made.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' account page requests failed, and the share of requests failing rose well above its usual level.

Account page requests were raising ZeroDivisionError in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py at line {F1.1}, logged over {G5309.3}. The ClientDisconnected failures were logged only over {G46bc.3}, before the onset.

Account pages had moved from the legacy renderer to the new renderer, which served the most pages at {Gc27d.11}. The flag reads show legacy-checkout-fallback mostly off at {G7ad6.6} and off over {G7037.4}.

ruled_out.what: The monthly-spend-feature flag, switched on by admin at the same instant: turning it back off left the service at the incident's level, so it was put back on.
A deploy: no deploys came back for the day before the onset.
The ClientDisconnected failures: they were logged only before the onset, and the failures from the onset on are ZeroDivisionError.

causal_chain.step: The feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback was switched off by admin at {P1.1}. Turning it back on brought the service out of the incident's level.
The new renderer's spend summary divides by a count that is zero for an ordinary shopper with no purchases this month, so its requests for those shoppers failed.

input.cause_in_plain_words: Switching off a setting moved shoppers' account pages onto a newer way of building them, and that newer way crashed by dividing by zero, likely for shoppers who have bought before but have bought nothing yet this month.

contributing_factors.factor: One flag change could move every account page from the legacy renderer to the new renderer at once. No gradual rollout or automatic rollback was seen on legacy-checkout-fallback.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A gradual, percentage-based rollout with rollback on error rate would have exposed only a small share of account pages to the failing path, and it would have been undone automatically.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: No check was seen that ran the new renderer's spend summary against a shopper with past purchases but none this month before the flag change sent account pages to it. Code-Fix says its new tests for that case would fail against the current code.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Such a check would likely have failed before legacy-checkout-fallback was switched off, and the change would have been held back.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

contributing_factors.factor: The HighErrorRate alert on io-shop was linked to no on-call incident, so nobody was paged.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: An on-call person would have been engaged on the alert and could have acted on the switched-off flag alongside Argus.
contributing_factors.label: CF-3

contributing_factors.factor: Admin made two flag changes on the service at the same instant, so the record could not tell which one set off the errors.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: With only one change at the onset, the right flag would have been reverted first and the service restored without first trying the wrong one.
contributing_factors.label: CF-4

lead_effects.effect: It did not change what was done: the investigation weighed it as unverified and ranked legacy-checkout-fallback second, so Argus reverted that flag only after the monthly-spend-feature revert was refuted, and the confirmed action then bore the lead out.

went_well.item: A person in the incident's thread named legacy-checkout-fallback, the flag the confirmed action later showed was the one that mattered.
The Investigator Agent read the metrics, the production changes and the logs, and formed candidate causes that covered both flag changes.
The Mitigation Agent put monthly-spend-feature back ON once reverting it did not help, so no unneeded change was left in place.
The Mitigation Agent turned legacy-checkout-fallback back ON.
The Mitigation Agent confirmed that the service was no longer at the incident's level.
The Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as draft pull request #432.

went_wrong: The investigation ranked monthly-spend-feature first and Argus reverted it first. Yet the logs it had read showed account pages moving from the legacy renderer to the new renderer at the onset, and a person in the thread had named legacy-checkout-fallback, so the flag that restored the service was reverted only after the first revert was refuted.

input.root_cause: In `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, the monthly spend summary divides the account's total for the month by the number of purchases it made this month (line {F1.1}). That number is zero for an ordinary shopper who has bought before but not this month. Switching legacy-checkout-fallback off sent account pages to the new renderer, whose spend summary reaches this division, and `serve_account_page` turns the resulting ZeroDivisionError into a failed page.
input.still_at_risk: Switching the legacy-checkout-fallback flag off again would send account pages back to the new renderer and fail them again.
